Kept separate from the owner controller and the {@code Owner} model so the rule 22 * lives in one place, as pure functions with no web or persistence dependencies. Mirrors 23 * {@link LocalityResolver} (which supplies the region) and {@link LuhnCheckDigit}. 24 * 25 *

The code is {@code '-'}: REGION is the region derived from the owner's postcode 26 * (see {@link LocalityResolver#resolveFromPostcode}) and HASH8 is the first eight upper-case 27 * hexadecimal characters of the SHA-256 digest of the owner's normalized telephone concatenated with 28 * the last name. It carries no sequence number, so two distinct people always receive distinct codes 29 * only insofar as their {@code (telephone, lastName)} pairs differ. 30 */ 31 public abstract class CustomerCode { 32 33 /** Separates the region and hash components of the code. */ 34 private static final String SEPARATOR = "-"; 35 36 /** Number of leading hex characters of the SHA-256 digest kept as the HASH8 component. */ 37 private static final int HASH_LENGTH = 8; 38 39 /** 40 * Build a customer code {@code '-'} from an owner's region, telephone and last name. 41 * 42 * @param region the region code (e.g. {@code NSW}, or {@code UNKNOWN}) 43 * @param telephone the owner's normalized telephone, or null 44 * @param lastName the owner's last name, or null 45 * @return the customer code 46 */ 47 public static String of(String region, String telephone, String lastName) { 48 return region + SEPARATOR + hash8(telephone, lastName); 49 } 50 51 /** 52 * The region (the part before the {@code '-'}) of a customer code, or {@code null} when the code is 53 * {@code null}. This is how the owner's locality is now derived from its identity. 54 * 55 * @param customerCode a customer code, or null 56 * @return the region component, or null 57 */ 58 public static String region(String customerCode) { 59 if (customerCode == null) { 60 return null; 61 } 62 int separator = customerCode.indexOf(SEPARATOR); 63 return separator < 0 ? customerCode : customerCode.substring(0, separator); 64 } 65 66 /** 67 * First eight upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over {@code (telephone + lastName)}, each part 68 * treated as the empty string when absent. 69 */ 70 private static String hash8(String telephone, String lastName) { 71 String telephonePart = telephone == null ? "" : telephone; 72 String lastNamePart = lastName == null ? "" : lastName; 73 return Sha256.hex(telephonePart + lastNamePart).substring(0, HASH_LENGTH).toUpperCase(); 74 } 75 76 } 77

Kept separate from the owner controller and the {@code Owner} model so the 24 * rule for deciding when two owners denote the same person lives in one place, as pure functions 25 * with no web or persistence dependencies. Mirrors {@link TelephoneNormalizer}, 26 * {@link EmailNormalizer} and {@link Soundex}, whose comparison keys it composes. 27 * 28 *

The key is the SHA-256 hex digest of the owner's normalized telephone, lower-cased email (or 29 * the empty string when absent) and the {@linkplain Soundex#soundex Soundex} of their last name, 30 * joined with {@code '|'} separators before hashing: 31 * {@code sha256hex(normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + soundex(lastName))}. Two owners 32 * are the same, and a create is rejected as a {@code 409 Conflict}, only when their whole keys are 33 * equal — so the previously separate telephone, email and household duplicate checks are all 34 * subsumed by this one key. Because the telephone is part of the key, two owners who share a last 35 * name and postcode but carry different telephones have different keys: they are not a hard 36 * duplicate but a {@linkplain OwnerIdentity soft match}. Only an exact full-key match is a 37 * duplicate. 38 */ 39 public abstract class OwnerIdentity { 40 41 /** Separates the telephone, email and last-name components hashed into the key. */ 42 private static final String SEPARATOR = "|"; 43 44 /** 45 * Builds the identity key from an owner's raw parts. The telephone and email are reduced to 46 * their {@linkplain TelephoneNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} / 47 * {@linkplain EmailNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} forms and the last name to its 48 * {@linkplain Soundex#soundex Soundex} code so values stored in different shapes still compose 49 * equal keys; an absent (null or blank) email contributes the empty string, and an absent last 50 * name codes to the empty string. The joined parts are then reduced to a 51 * {@linkplain Sha256#hex SHA-256} hex digest. 52 * 53 * @param telephone the owner's telephone (normalized on create), or null 54 * @param email the owner's email (lower-cased on create), or null/blank when absent 55 * @param lastName the owner's last name, or null 56 * @return the owner's identity key, a 64-character lower-case hex SHA-256 digest 57 */ 58 public static String identityKey(String telephone, String email, String lastName) { 59 String telephonePart = telephone == null ? "" : TelephoneNormalizer.toComparisonKey(telephone); 60 String emailPart = (email == null || email.isBlank()) ? "" : EmailNormalizer.toComparisonKey(email); 61 String lastNamePart = Soundex.soundex(lastName); 62 return Sha256.hex(telephonePart + SEPARATOR + emailPart + SEPARATOR + lastNamePart); 63 } 64 65 /** 66 * Builds the identity key from a persisted owner's stored telephone, email and last name. 67 * 68 * @param owner the owner (non-null) 69 * @return the owner's identity key 70 */ 71 public static String identityKey(Owner owner) { 72 return identityKey(owner.getTelephone(), owner.getEmail(), owner.getLastName()); 73 } 74 75 } 76

Kept separate from the owner controller and the 24 * {@code Owner} model so the rule lives in one place, as a pure function with no web or persistence 25 * dependencies. Mirrors {@link BusinessDayAdjuster}, whose business-day-adjusted date this is 26 * derived from. 27 * 28 *

The fiscal year starts on 1 July and is identified by the calendar year in which it ends: a 29 * date on or after 1 July belongs to the fiscal year of {@code year + 1}, and a date before 1 July 30 * belongs to the fiscal year of {@code year}. So 2026-09-04 falls in fiscal year 2027 and 2026-03-04 31 * falls in fiscal year 2026. The {@linkplain #label label} form is {@code FY} followed by the last 32 * two digits of that year, e.g. {@code FY27}. 33 */ 34 public abstract class FiscalYear { 35 36 /** 37 * The fiscal year (as a full calendar year) that {@code date} falls in. The fiscal year starts 38 * on 1 July and is named for the calendar year in which it ends. 39 * 40 * @param date the date (must not be null) 41 * @return the fiscal year, e.g. {@code 2027} for 2026-09-04 42 */ 43 public static int yearOf(LocalDate date) { 44 return date.getMonthValue() >= Month.JULY.getValue() ? date.getYear() + 1 : date.getYear(); 45 } 46 47 /** 48 * The {@code FY} label of the fiscal year {@code date} falls in, where {@code YY} is the last 49 * two digits of the fiscal year, zero-padded. 50 * 51 * @param date the date (must not be null) 52 * @return the fiscal year label, e.g. {@code FY27} for 2026-09-04 53 */ 54 public static String label(LocalDate date) { 55 return String.format("FY%02d", yearOf(date) % 100); 56 } 57 58 /** 59 * The number of fiscal years elapsed between two dates, i.e. the number of 1-July boundaries 60 * crossed from {@code from} to {@code to}. 61 * 62 * @param from the earlier date (must not be null) 63 * @param to the later date (must not be null) 64 * @return {@code yearOf(to) - yearOf(from)} 65 */ 66 public static int elapsed(LocalDate from, LocalDate to) { 67 return yearOf(to) - yearOf(from); 68 } 69 70 } 71

It serializes to the JSON object 26 * {@code {seq, ownerId, customerCode, membershipLevel, event:'OWNER_CREATED'}}. 27 * 28 *

{@code seq} is a monotonically increasing integer across creates, letting a consumer order and 29 * de-duplicate events. {@code customerCode} carries the owner's current primary identifier: 30 * today an owner is keyed by its {@code customerCode}, and when that identifier is later unified into 31 * the {@code memberId} the event simply carries the memberId in its place (the controller derives the 32 * value through a single accessor, {@code primaryIdentifier}, so only that one place changes). 33 * 34 *

The event is a record, so it is immutable once constructed: its fields cannot be mutated after 35 * the create that produced it, which is the guarantee an audit trail depends on. 36 */ 37 public record OwnerCreatedEvent(long seq, Integer ownerId, String customerCode, Integer membershipLevel) { 38 39 /** Fixed discriminator identifying this kind of audit event. */ 40 static final String EVENT_TYPE = "OWNER_CREATED"; 41 42 private static final ObjectMapper MAPPER = JsonMapper.builder().build(); 43 44 /** 45 * Renders this event as its canonical JSON representation, with fields in the documented order 46 * {@code {seq, ownerId, customerCode, membershipLevel, event}}. This is the exact string published 47 * to the {@code AUDIT} logger. 48 * 49 * @return the event as a single-line JSON object 50 */ 51 public String toJson() { 52 ObjectNode node = MAPPER.createObjectNode(); 53 node.put("seq", this.seq); 54 node.put("ownerId", this.ownerId); 55 node.put("customerCode", this.customerCode); 56 node.put("membershipLevel", this.membershipLevel); 57 node.put("event", EVENT_TYPE); 58 return MAPPER.writeValueAsString(node); 59 } 60 } 61

## What I did

Preparatory, behavior-preserving refactors that pull the future change into the named hotspots so it lands as a small, natural diff:

**`OwnerMapper.java`** — the region of the identifier was derived independently in three places (`locality` mapping, `timezone()`, `ownerSegment()`), each calling `CustomerCode.region(owner.getCustomerCode())`.
- Collapsed all three onto one `locality(owner)` accessor. When `memberId` replaces `customerCode`, only this one method changes to parse the region out of the new format — `timezone` and `ownerSegment` follow automatically.
- Extracted the inline `fiscalYear` mapping expression into a `fiscalYear(owner)` method, giving the "fiscal-year value must reference the memberId" requirement a single home to edit.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — `addOwner` was already large and carried the two `AUDIT` emissions inline (the human line references `customerCode`/`membershipNumber`; the event goes through `primaryIdentifier`).
- Extracted both into one `emitOwnerCreatedAudit(owner, ownerDto)` helper (same order, `EVENT_SEQ` still bumped exactly once). The audit trail's view of owner identity now changes in one focused spot instead of inside the orchestration method. `primaryIdentifier` was already the intended single seam, so I left it.

**`CustomerCode.java`** — the new `memberId` HASH8 is explicitly "the same SHA-256-over-(telephone+lastName) first-8-hex used by the region-and-hash identity."
- Promoted the private `hash8(telephone, lastName)` to a public building block (with `of(...)` still delegating to it), so the future member-id composition reuses it instead of duplicating the digest logic inside `generateMemberId`.

I did not touch the `checkDigit`/`membershipNumber` mappings, the `Owner` fields, the OpenAPI schema, or `OwnerCreatedEvent` — those are removals/renames that belong to the change itself, not to the groundwork.
